Level H

Checkpoints: Save & Load

Convert your objects to data and back again

What You'll Learn

1 Serialise object state to a dictionary
2 Deserialise a dictionary back into an object
3 Use class methods (@classmethod) for factories
4 Separate data storage from file I/O

Key Terms

Term Definition
Serialisation Converting an object into a storable format (like a dictionary)
Deserialisation Reconstructing an object from stored data
Round-trip The process of saving and then loading to verify data integrity
Class Method A method bound to the class (cls) rather than an instance (self)

Serialisation Hooks

Player
+ to_save_data() → dict
+ from_save_data(cls, data) → Player
to_save_data: Packs stats into a dictionary.
from_save_data: Unpacks dictionary into a new Player.

Structure Guide

Implement these hooks to let the engine save your game.

1 to_save_data (Instance Method)
METHOD to_save_data() → dict:
Return a dictionary containing all stats needed to restore the player:
  • name, player_type, health, max_health, armour, accuracy
  • inventory (list of items)
RETURN { "name": self.name, ... }
2 from_save_data (@classmethod)
@CLASSMETHOD
METHOD from_save_data(cls, data) → Player:
Important: This creates a NEW player.
  1. Create instance: player = cls(data["name"])
  2. Restore functionality: calls __init__ automatically
  3. Overwrite stats: player.health = data["health"], etc.
  4. Restore inventory: Loop through data["inventory"] and add items
  5. Return the new player object

Your Mission

Enable Persistence

Don't lose your progress! Implement the save/load hooks so the engine can store your player data.

Use the save and load commands in the game to test it.
